hero.title: Small business invoicing software for teams that sell their time
hero.description: If your business bills clients by the hour, your invoices should come straight from those hours. We built Paidlyo so a small team can send an accurate invoice in minutes, not lose an evening to it at month end.
painPoints.1.title: The hours are in three different places
painPoints.1.text: One person keeps a spreadsheet, another writes times in a notebook, and the rest is in someone's head. By the time you add it all up, a few billable hours have quietly gone missing.
painPoints.2.title: Month end eats a whole day
painPoints.2.text: Copying hours into an invoice template line by line is slow and easy to get wrong. So invoices go out late, and late invoices tend to get paid late.
painPoints.3.title: You're never quite sure who has paid
painPoints.3.text: A client pays half now and promises the rest next week. A month later nobody remembers what is still open until you dig through bank statements.
painPoints.4.title: Big software for a small problem
painPoints.4.text: A lot of invoicing tools come bundled with accounting, inventory and payroll. If you just need to bill your hours, that is a lot of setup for features you will never open.

features.1.title: Invoices built from your tracked hours
features.1.text: Pick a client and Paidlyo drafts the invoice from every hour you haven't billed yet. Group the lines by project, task or person, and edit anything before you send it.
features.2.title: The right rate on every line
features.2.text: Set hourly rates per project and per task once. After that, nobody on the team has to remember which job is billed at which rate.
features.3.title: A clear view of what's still owed
features.3.text: Record full or partial payments as they come in. The outstanding invoices report sorts what is unpaid by age, so the oldest debts are at the top.
features.4.title: One price that grows with the team
features.4.text: Every feature is included for $9 per person a month. A team of five pays $45 a month, with unlimited clients, projects and invoices.
faq.1.question: Is there a free version for small businesses?
faq.1.answer: There is no free plan. Every account starts with a 14-day free trial, and after that it is $9 per person a month or $90 per person a year. A card is needed to start, but nothing is charged until the trial ends.
faq.2.question: Does Paidlyo work if my business sells products?
faq.2.answer: Not really. Paidlyo builds invoices from tracked hours and has no product catalog or inventory. If most of what you sell is physical goods, an invoicing-first tool will fit better.
faq.3.question: Can my clients pay by card straight from the invoice?
faq.3.answer: No. Clients open the invoice through a private link, with no login, and pay you the usual way, for example by bank transfer. You then record the payment in Paidlyo.
faq.4.question: Can I bill clients in different currencies?
faq.4.answer: Yes. Each client has their own currency, so a client abroad gets an invoice in the currency you agreed with them.

painPoints.3.title: Time-based or item-based: which kind of invoicing fits your business
painPoints.3.text: Small businesses bill in two very different ways. Some sell items: a product, a fixed-price package, a delivery. Their invoice is a list of things with a price next to each one. Others sell time. Their invoice is a list of hours, and the hard part is making sure every hour is counted at the right rate. | Paidlyo is built for the second group. We start from the hours your team tracked and build the invoice from them. That makes it a good fit for an IT support company, a small marketing or design team, a bookkeeping practice, a consultancy or any team of two to twenty people that bills by the hour. | It is honestly not the right tool if you mostly sell physical products, need an inventory list, or want clients to pay by card from inside the invoice. In those cases an invoicing-first or accounting tool will save you more time than we can.
example.rows.1.label: How to invoice clients for hours, step by step
example.rows.1.value: Whatever tool you use, hourly invoices go smoother when the groundwork is done before the invoice exists. This is the routine we recommend to small teams. | In Paidlyo, steps 2 to 4 happen as you work, and step 5 is one click: choose the client and the draft is ready, grouped by project, task or person. You then edit any line that needs a clearer description before you share it.
example.rows.2.label: Agree the rates and payment terms in writing before the work starts, so the invoice holds no surprises | Track time on the same day, while you still remember what the work was | Write entry notes the client will understand, such as 'Fixed printer drivers on 3 office PCs' rather than just 'Support' | Mark internal work, like team meetings or travel, as non-billable instead of deleting it | Invoice on a fixed day each month, for example the first working day | Read the draft once as if you were the client, then send it with a clear due date
example.rows.4.label: Getting paid on time when you're a small team
example.rows.4.value: In a small business, one late payment can be felt in payroll the same month. Most late payments are not bad faith. The invoice was unclear, arrived late, or simply got buried, and nobody followed up. | Paidlyo helps with the follow-up part. When money arrives, you record it against the invoice, in full or in part, and the balance updates. The outstanding invoices report lists everything unpaid by age, so a five-minute weekly check shows you exactly who to call first.
example.total.label: Send invoices the same week the work is done, not when you find time | Use short, plain payment terms, such as Net 15 or Net 30, and state the due date as a date | Show hours and rate on every line so the client can approve it without questions | Record partial payments as soon as they land, so nobody chases money already paid | Check the outstanding list every week and follow up the oldest invoice first
